explanation: The L76V mutation reduces a branched leucine to the smaller valine in the flap region, creating a cavity approximately 27 Ų in volume that is 7 Å from darunavir. Though the mutation doesn't directly contact the inhibitor, this loss of hydrophobic bulk disrupts the precise packing architecture of the flap domain that normally stabilizes the inhibitor-bound conformation. The resulting conformational flexibility of the flap allows darunavir to sample suboptimal binding geometries, reducing binding enthalpy despite maintaining similar electrostatic properties.
